sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate faithfully encodes the conditional requirement: it targets the supplied ship owner, checks sea-ice origin, integer winter growth count <= 1, decimal thickness from 0.3 m through 2.0 m inclusive, requires firstYearIce when the antecedent is present, and rejects every other classification including alongside firstYearIce. No unconditional input constraints, wrong-owner paths, invented terms, or vocabulary issues remain.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The conditional logic is not fully faithful for multi-valued classifications: FILTER NOT EXISTS for the required firstYearIce value passes when both firstYearIce and a different iceTypeClassification value are present. Under the applicable origin, growth, and thickness conditions, reject any classification value other than nltl:firstYearIce (and reject absence of the required value), using a portable SHACL Core/SPARQL constraint without OPTIONAL inside FILTER NOT EXISTS. All supplied canonical terms, owners, paths, thresholds, datatypes, and units are otherwise appropriate.

Repair the unresolved prior classification constraint and preserve that instruction: under the applicable origin, growth, and thickness conditions, require nltl:firstYearIce and reject every other nltl:iceTypeClassification value using a portable conditional SHACL Core/SPARQL formulation. Also remove the unconditional sh:minCount and numeric range constraints on nltl:winterGrowthCount and nltl:iceThickness: the requirement is an implication, so those inputs and bounds must be checked only when the complete antecedent is present, not imposed on every ship. Keep the supplied ship owners, canonical terms, thresholds, datatypes, and metre unit.

The candidate faithfully encodes the conditional requirement: it targets the supplied ship owner, checks sea-ice origin, integer winter growth count <= 1, decimal thickness from 0.3 m through 2.0 m inclusive, requires firstYearIce when the antecedent is present, and rejects every other classification including alongside firstYearIce. No unconditional input constraints, wrong-owner paths, invented terms, or vocabulary issues remain.
